sources.entry: MakLock - Lock any macOS app with Touch ID, Apple Watch proximity, or password. Full-screen blur overlay on all monitors. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/dutkiewiczmaciej/MakLock) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
MakLock - Free macOS menu bar app that locks applications with Touch ID, Apple Watch proximity, or password using a full-screen blur overlay.

summary.one_liner: MakLock is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that locks other applications behind Touch ID, Apple Watch proximity, or a password, shown with a full-screen blur overlay.
summary.what_it_does: MakLock watches for launches and activations of protected apps via NSWorkspace and blocks access with a blur overlay on all displays until the user authenticates. Authentication options are Touch ID (single prompt), Apple Watch proximity with wrist detection, or a backup password for Macs without Touch ID. It can auto-lock after a configurable idle timeout and on sleep/wake, auto-close inactive protected apps, and close protected apps on sleep. A panic key (Cmd+Opt+Shift+Ctrl+U) dismisses overlays, and a system blacklist (Terminal, Xcode, Activity Monitor and similar) prevents those apps from being locked. The README compares it against AppLocker and Cisdem AppCrypt, which it describes as sandboxed or trial-limited alternatives.
use_cases: Lock personal apps like Messages on a shared Mac
Hide app content from people looking over your shoulder
Prevent notification snooping by auto-closing idle apps
Require Touch ID to open a sensitive app
Protect apps on a shared laptop when stepping away
how_to_run: Build and run with Cmd+R (requires Xcode 15+ and macOS 13+)
notable: Non-activating NSPanel overlay that does not steal focus, avoiding content flash on launch
Re-locks on quit: Cmd+Q clears authentication so the next launch requires re-auth
Apple Watch proximity unlock with wrist detection and auto-relock when the watch leaves range
Distributed outside the App Store for full overlay and process management, signed and notarized
Timeout failsafe auto-dismisses overlays after 60 seconds without interaction
caveats: Requires macOS 13.0 (Ventura) or later; Apple Watch unlock requires watchOS 9+ and is optional
Trusted Wi-Fi auto-unlock and per-window overlay are listed as planned for v1.1 and v1.2
Distributed outside the App Store, so it is not sandboxed
